dedupe_keys.name: event duration monitoring storm overflows annual returns england

description: This Environment Agency dataset reports how often and for how long each monitored storm overflow in England discharged in a year. The 10 Water and Sewerage Companies submit Event Duration Monitoring (EDM) data in their regulatory Annual Return, as a condition of their permits to discharge under the Environmental Permitting Regulations. Files are published per year (2020 to 2025) with a sheet for each company, listing spill counts and durations per overflow; from 2021 they also give reasons why monitors covered less than 90 per cent of the return period and why an overflow had high spill counts. Each year adds summary tables (overflows with monitors, average spill count and duration per company), a README guide explains the fields, and a sixth file carries long-term trends from 2016 to 2025. Coverage is England at the resolution of individual overflows, in British National Grid. Access: free ZIP downloads from the Defra Data Services Platform and data.gov.uk, plus a spill frequency web map, under the Open Government Licence with Environment Agency attribution; updated annually, with a revision on 20 August 2026 after quality checks of Anglian Water and Northumbrian Water data. Caveats: figures are what companies held at submission, some derived metrics were not recalculated after corrections, and the separate start/stop event data are not verified by the Agency. Simulation uses: calibrating sewer and drainage models against observed spills, assessing hazard exposure of receiving waters and planning overflow reduction under climate change. Related records: the UWWTD treatment plants dataset (data-uwwtd-treatment-plants) and the Bellinge benchmark (data-bellinge-urban-drainage-dataset).
